notes: v6 = v5 with one universe change, made at Ajeeb's request on 2026-11-16: a token can be traded from 3 hours after launch instead of 3 days (universe.min_age_days 3 to 0.125). His hypothesis: the volume in young tokens is genuine, so a young token with serious buyers and sellers should be considered. Every other test still applies to it: $50k liquidity, $100k of 24-hour volume, 500 trades, the market-cap band, the RugCheck screen, and the entry rules (300 trades in the last hour, more buyers than sellers, rising volume). What the record says, hints only: replayed on the recorded snapshots the change adds 7 trades on 6 tokens under 3 days old, 4 wins, +4.2% a trade, with stops filling at -20% to -26% instead of about -15%; a buy at any moment in a token 6 to 24 hours old made -2.5%, and 6% of those positions were in tokens that left the record while held. The data cannot tell genuine volume from bots; the paper results will show whether it pays. Judge young tokens apart (python3 -m bot.report, 'By age of the token at entry'). v5 = v4 with entry.min_txns_h1 150 to 300 (2026-11-16 06:30 UTC review; a signal on a thinly traded token has been reliably bad). Exit, portfolio, safety, costs and discovery are unchanged since v4. See reviews/LESSONS.md for the evidence and what would prove each change wrong. Every threshold is still an untested guess. Change one section at a time and bump 'version' on every edit so trades can be traced to the rules that produced them.
